test.name: First plan for q_001 plans from loc_001 counted collections without re-running collections_search
test.description: Same state as ut_research_plan_005, but loc_001 carries the six Pennsylvania collections locality-guide saved, each with a person_count. research-plan must plan from those collections and make no collections_search call for Schuylkill or Pennsylvania (the call would return the same state-scoped set); the national United States call for the federal census stays allowed. Issue #3545 lead 3: in 6 of 10 post-#3860 e2e runs research-plan repeated locality-guide's collections_search on the place it had just surveyed.

input.delegation:
Create a research plan for the parentage question.

questionId: q_001
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: A `localities` entry (loc_001) for Schuylkill County / Pennsylvania is ALREADY in research.json — the orchestrator ran locality-guide before research-plan. The skill should READ that entry and use its facts/quirks; it should NOT call wiki_search / wiki_place_page / place_population (research-plan no longer holds those tools — the know-how comes from the localities entry). Do NOT fail it for not surveying.

The plan must show it READ loc_001, and the persisted `plan_items[].rationale` is the only place that counts — narration is not persisted and search-records never sees it, so a response text that names loc_001 while the rationales do not is a fail on this point. Read the persisted plan items, not the prose. What counts as evidence of reading: the `loc_001` id itself, or a fact distinctive to that entry — county formation in 1811, probate from 1811 at the county Register of Wills, Catholic parishes staying under Philadelphia until the Diocese of Allentown in 1961, or the browse-only anthracite-region films. Statewide PA vital registration from 1906 does NOT count: any model states it without opening the entry, so a plan that cites only that has not shown it read anything.

loc_001's `collections[]` carry person_count, and those counts are the availability source for Pennsylvania and Schuylkill collections: describe 1999196 (person_count 0) as browse-only, the others as name-searchable. A collections_search call on Schuylkill or Pennsylvania repeats locality-guide's survey and is a fail on this point (a deterministic validator also checks it); collections_search on "United States" for the federal census, volume_search, place_search, project_context and research_query (external_collections) are expected, not violations.
Plan items must include rationale explaining why each record type was chosen for the parentage question — generic rationale ('more records would help') is a fail.

At least one item should target a post-1850 census (1870, 1880, or 1900) to track Patrick into adulthood; the 1880 census relationship column is the best direct parentage indicator in the available fixtures.
